CVE-2026-116225.title: Quadratic CPU Denial of Service in SNMP BER Object Identifier Sub-Identifier Decoding
CVE-2026-116225.description:
Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the BER decoder in Erlang/OTP snmp allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust CPU via an SNMP message that contains an OBJECT IDENTIFIER with a very long sub-identifier.

snmp_pdus:dec_oid_element/3 does not limit the number of base-128 octets in a sub-identifier, and snmp_pdus:dec_oid_elements/3 does not limit the number of sub-identifiers, so one sub-identifier can span the whole datagram. When the value exceeds the native integer size, each further octet copies a growing bignum, and decoding time grows quadratically with the sub-identifier length. The agent and the manager decode OIDs before they check community strings or SNMPv3 credentials, inside the single network interface process (snmpa_net_if or snmpm_net_if). That process does not read the next datagram until decoding completes.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to snmp from…

In server mode pgAdmin 4 validates a path a user gives for a file in their storage directory with check_access_permission() and then opened it by name. A symbolic link swapped in at the file or at any parent directory between the check and the open redirected the operation outside the storage directory, so a file could be written, overwritten or read, or loaded into a table, as the operating-system account running pgAdmin. CVE-2026-135389.description: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. CVE-2026-99706.title: mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs
CVE-2026-99706.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs

numa_rebuild_large_mapping() and do_swap_page() can be tricked into
generating an address wraparound, crashing the kernel. All that's required
is to map a tail page of a large folio close enough to the start/end of
the address space to e.g., make

unsigned long addr_start = addr - (nr << PAGE_SHIFT);

to wrap around.

Let's fix it by providing a better helper, folio_scan_range(), that
takes care of staying within VMA and page table boundaries while
handling possible wraparounds.

There are some nasty details, like not being able to use pmd_addr_end()
in this context. Add some helpful comments for these cases.
